ancestors.notes: Descent from Proto-Iranian via Old Persian and Middle Persian (Pahlavi) to New Persian.
Arabic adstrate: after the Islamic conquest a very large lexical layer entered New Persian (and the Perso-Arabic script), though core phonology and grammar stayed Iranian.

name: Persian (Farsi)
notes: Tehran standard. Many Arabic emphatic/pharyngeal consonants have merged with plain counterparts. 6-vowel system: /ɒː, æ, e, o, iː, uː/ (Windfuhr 1979/2009; Majidi & Ternes 1991 JIPA illustration; Toosarvandani 2004). GOLD-CONVENTION DIVERGENCE: the WikiPron 'fa' gold set transcribes long ā with plain 'a'/'aː' and the rhotic with plain 'r' rather than the tap 'ɾ', and omits the word-initial glottal onset this spec supplies for vowel-initial words (e.g. gold 'آری'→'aːreː' vs this spec's phonemically correct 'ʔɒːɾ(iː)'). That WikiPron convention matches an older/transliteration-flavored broad transcription, not the phonetic value described by the cited standard references, so this spec intentionally does NOT chase it — see tests/test_fa_convention.py. Separately, WikiPron entries also carry short vowels that are simply unwritten in Perso-Arabic orthography (an abjad); no G2P over bare script can recover these without a pronunciation lexicon, which is out of scope here.
